falmouth.s1_head: Kitting the events trade of the Fal
s1loc: Falmouth's live scene runs from the Princess Pavilion on Melville Road, a Victorian hall and gardens staging music, comedy and theatre, to the open waterfront arena of Events Square at Discovery Quay beside the National Maritime Museum Cornwall. The Falmouth International Sea Shanty Festival fills the harbour each June across the Seasalt Stage on Events Square, the Princess Pavilion bandstand and around twenty town venues, while Falmouth Week takes over the waterfront every August with racing, stages and a packed crew calendar.

And the trade here runs at two very different sizes. The maritime museum, the bigger festival organisers and the production companies serving the regatta and shanty weekends run sizeable seasonal teams and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers around the Fal want just a few embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier on this stretch of Cornish coast has to serve the packed festival weekend and the single crew alike, which is why we keep trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

The calendar runs well past the summer regattas, with the Falmouth Oyster Festival each October bringing demonstration stages, marquees and street food to Events Square and Discovery Quay, and the town's pubs and quayside venues carrying live music the year round. Sitting at the mouth of the Fal with Truro, Camborne and Penzance all within reach, Falmouth feeds stage, rigging and front-of-house work out across west Cornwall, widening the catchment of crews needing branded event and steward kit.

Indoor performances run from the Centenary Methodist Church, which hosts the long-running Camborne Music Festival every November, to Tyacks Hotel on Commercial Street, a Grade II listed coaching inn that stands as the town's home for live music and local life.

And the trade here works at two scales. The Trevithick Day organisers, the festival committees and the production companies serving the bigger crowd days run seasonal crews and order branded kit through managed accounts, while independent crews, promoters and entertainers across the old mining country want just a few embroidered polos or fleeces. A workwear supplier in this part of Cornwall has to serve the packed street-festival day and the single crew alike, which is why we keep trade accounts and direct online ordering side by side.

Camborne's identity is bound to its mining heritage, from Holman's engineering works to the engine houses of the Camborne and Redruth district, and that history feeds heritage days, parades and convoys that fill the calendar beyond Trevithick Day. With choirs and brass bands rooted deep in the town and Truro, Falmouth and Penzance all close by, Camborne draws stage, crew and front-of-house work from right across west Cornwall and the surrounding mining villages.
